history.dynasty: Pallavas (believed builders; first inscription 846 CE under Nandivarman III); later contributions by Medieval Cholas (Rajendra Chola I, Rajadhiraja Chola II, Rajaraja Chola III), Vijayanagara kings, Sambuvarayars and Madurai Nayaks
history.period: 7th-9th century CE (Pallava foundations); inscriptions from 846 CE onwards
history.summary: The Ulagalantha Perumal Temple at Kanchipuram is the Vamana/Trivikrama temple of the brief and one of the 108 Divya Desams. Historian Nagaswamy calls it Kanchipuram's oldest temple. It is believed to have been built by the Pallavas with later contributions from the Medieval Cholas, Vijayanagara kings and Madurai Nayaks; it carries 15 inscriptions from the Pallavas, Cholas and Sambuvarayars, the first dated 846 CE in the reign of Nandivarman III (846-869 CE). The legend: Vishnu incarnated as Vamana, the dwarf Brahmin, to quell the pride of asura king Mahabali; at Mahabali's request he appeared here in his giant form as Ulagalantha Perumal ('the Lord who measured the world'), the near-35-ft image with the left leg extended parallel to the ground. The temple is unique among Divya Desams: the complex houses FOUR Divya Desams - Tirukkaravanam, Tirukarakam, Tiruneerakam and Tiruooragam (the last within the sanctum sanctorum of the main temple). It is glorified in the Naalayira Divya Prabandham by Tirumangai Alvar and Thirumazhisai Aazhwar. The temple has a three-tiered raja gopuram with seven kalasams and is maintained by the Hindu Religious and Endowment Board of Tamil Nadu. CSV note: the CSV spelling 'Kancheepuram' is the anglicised variant; the file uses the standard spelling 'Kanchipuram'.

name: Ulagalantha Perumal Temple
town_description: Kanchipuram (Big Kanchipuram) is one of the seven sacred temple cities of India, in Kanchipuram district about 75 km from Chennai. The Ulagalantha Perumal Temple stands in central Kanchipuram close to the Kamakshi Amman Temple, in a city dense with Pallava and Chola-era shrines.
